question: The Harappan brought Gold from present-day _______ in India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Harappans obtained gold largely from sources within the Indian subcontinent, and the principal domestic source identified by archaeologists is present-day Karnataka, particularly the Kolar and Hutti gold fields. (हड़प्पावासी — कर्नाटक से सोना)

 

• Gold objects (beads, ornaments, foils) have been found at Harappan sites such as Mohenjodaro, Harappa, Lothal and Kalibangan, indicating an established trade network bringing gold from the south.

 

• Besides Karnataka, some gold is also believed to have come from Afghanistan and the northern regions, but Karnataka (South India) remains the most cited domestic source in Harappan trade studies.

 

• The Harappans were skilled in crafting jewellery, and gold ornaments recovered from these sites show advanced techniques like granulation and repoussé.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Harappans procured other raw materials too from specific regions: copper from Rajasthan (Khetri), tin possibly from Afghanistan, lapis lazuli from Badakshan (Afghanistan), and carnelian from Gujarat (Bharuch/Saurashtra).

 

• Lothal in Gujarat was an important port-town and bead-making/trading centre of the Harappan civilization.

 

NOTE

 

• Telangana (Option 1): Not identified as a principal Harappan gold source in standard archaeological accounts.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 2): Not associated with Harappan-era gold procurement.

 

• Kerala (Option 4): Not cited as a Harappan gold source; it lies further south and outside the usual trade routes described for the Harappan civilization.

question: Which of the following is NOT the component of the capital expenditure of the Government?
option_1: Expenditure on the acquisition of machinery
option_2: Expenditure on the acquisition of land
option_3: Expenditure on the acquisition of building
solution_text:
The correct answer is Interest payments.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Capital expenditure is spending that either creates an asset or reduces a liability, such as acquisition of land, buildings, machinery and equipment, and investment in shares, or loans and advances given by the government. (पूंजीगत व्यय — ब्याज भुगतान राजस्व व्यय है)

 

• Interest payments are a liability arising from past borrowings and are a recurring charge on the government's finances; they do not create any asset, so they are classified as revenue expenditure, not capital expenditure.

 

• Acquisition of machinery, land, and buildings all result in the creation of a physical/durable asset for the government, which is the defining feature of capital expenditure.

 

• In the Union Budget, capital expenditure is shown separately from revenue expenditure (which covers items like salaries, subsidies, pensions and interest payments).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major components of revenue expenditure include subsidies, salaries, pensions, and grants-in-aid for creation of assets.

 

• India's fiscal deficit is the excess of total expenditure (revenue + capital) over total receipts (excluding borrowings), and interest payments are one of the largest components of revenue expenditure in the Union Budget.

 

NOTE

 

• Expenditure on acquisition of machinery (Option 1): Creates a durable asset, hence capital expenditure.

 

• Expenditure on acquisition of land (Option 2): Creates/acquires an asset, hence capital expenditure.

 

• Expenditure on acquisition of building (Option 3): Creates a durable asset, hence capital expenditure.

question: Which of the following has become the first state in the country to get the L-root server?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rajasthan became the first state in India to get an L-root server, installed in Jaipur in 2022. (एल-रूट सर्वर — राजस्थान)

 

• The L-root server is one of the 13 logical root name servers of the global Domain Name System (DNS), operated by ICANN; it helps resolve domain names faster and improves internet resilience and speed within the region hosting it.

 

• It was set up through a collaboration between ICANN and India's National Internet Exchange of India (NIXI), in partnership with the Rajasthan government.

 

• Having a local root server instance reduces dependency on servers located abroad, improving internet speed, security and reliability for local users.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's first ICANN root server node was set up in New Delhi in 2017.

 

• There are only 13 named root server systems globally (A to M), though each is mirrored at many physical locations worldwide via anycast technology.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka (Option 1): Not the first state to get an L-root server.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 2): Not the first state to get an L-root server.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 4): Not the first state to get an L-root server.

question: Which minorities are mentioned in article 30 of the Indian Contituiton?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Linguistic and religious.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 30 of the Indian Constitution grants linguistic and religious minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice. (अनुच्छेद 30 — भाषायी और धार्मिक अल्पसंख्यक)

 

• Article 30(1) states: "All minorities, whether based on religion or language, shall have the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice."

 

• This right is a key part of the cultural and educational rights guaranteed under Part III (Fundamental Rights) of the Constitution, specifically Articles 29-30.

 

• Article 30(2) further ensures the State shall not discriminate against any educational institution in granting aid merely because it is under the management of a linguistic or religious minority.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 29 protects the interests of minorities by guaranteeing them the right to conserve their distinct language, script and culture.

 

• Articles 29 and 30 together form the constitutional safeguards for cultural and educational rights of minorities in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Religious, cultural and linguistic (Option 2): "Cultural" is not the term used in Article 30; the article specifically covers religious and linguistic minorities.

 

• Cultural and linguistic (Option 3): Omits "religious", which is explicitly named in Article 30, and wrongly includes "cultural".

 

• Religious and cultural (Option 4): Incorrectly substitutes "cultural" for "linguistic", which is the term actually used in Article 30.

question: Which of the following climate type is found under the cold climates?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tundra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the standard classification of world climates used in Indian geography texts, climates are grouped as Tropical, Dry, Warm Temperate, Cool Temperate, Cold climates, and Highland climates. The Tundra type falls under the Cold climate group. (टुंड्रा — शीत जलवायु)

 

• Cold climates are characterised by very low temperatures for most of the year, minimal vegetation (mosses, lichens), and permanently or seasonally frozen subsoil (permafrost), all typical of Tundra regions found in the Arctic fringes of North America, Europe and Asia.

 

• Humid subtropical and Humid continental climates belong to the Warm Temperate and Cool Temperate climate groups respectively, not the Cold climate group.

 

• Highland climate is treated as a separate category altogether, since its characteristics depend on altitude rather than latitude.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Tundra climate is found in the northern parts of Canada, Alaska, Siberia and Scandinavia, and is marked by extremely short, cool summers and long, severe winters.

 

• The Koppen climate classification similarly places Tundra (ET) under the broader Polar/Cold climate group, distinct from the Humid Continental (Dfa/Dfb) climates of the Cool Temperate group.

 

NOTE

 

• Humid subtropical (Option 1): Belongs to the Warm Temperate (Mesothermal) climate group, not Cold climates.

 

• Highland (Option 2): Forms its own separate climate category based on altitude, not part of the Cold climate group.

 

• Humid continental (Option 3): Belongs to the Cool Temperate (Microthermal) climate group, not the Cold climate group.

question: The Hindu College was established in Banaras in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1791.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The institution popularly referenced here (also known as the Government Sanskrit College, Banaras, later merged into Banaras Hindu University) was established in 1791 by Jonathan Duncan, the British Resident at Banaras. (बनारस हिंदू कॉलेज/संस्कृत कॉलेज — स्थापना वर्ष 1791)

 

• The college was set up to promote the study of Hindu law, philosophy and Sanskrit literature among Indians under British administration, and became one of the earliest centres of oriental learning in colonial India.

 

• Jonathan Duncan established the college with the objective of preserving and encouraging Sanskrit learning and Hindu religious/legal scholarship.

 

• This 1791 foundation later evolved through various stages into what became associated with Banaras Hindu University (BHU), founded much later in 1916 by Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Banaras Hindu University (BHU) itself was founded in 1916 by Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya, distinct from this earlier 1791 Sanskrit/Hindu College.

 

• Other notable colonial-era educational institutions include the Calcutta Madrasa (1781) by Warren Hastings and the Fort William College (1800) by Lord Wellesley.

 

NOTE

 

• 1771 (Option 1): Not the founding year of the Hindu/Sanskrit College at Banaras.

 

• 1801 (Option 2): Not the founding year; this is close to the year Fort William College was established (1800), a different institution.

 

• 1781 (Option 3): This is the founding year of the Calcutta Madrasa, not the Banaras Hindu/Sanskrit College.

question: The mass number of potassium is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 39.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Potassium (K) has an atomic number of 19, meaning it has 19 protons; its most abundant, stable isotope has 20 neutrons, giving it a mass number of 39 (19 protons + 20 neutrons). (पोटैशियम — द्रव्यमान संख्या 39)

 

• The mass number of an element is the sum of the number of protons and neutrons in its nucleus, and is generally taken from the most common/stable naturally occurring isotope unless otherwise specified.

 

• Potassium's standard atomic weight (~39.098 u) reflects the natural abundance-weighted average of its isotopes, of which Potassium-39 is by far the most abundant (about 93%).

 

• Potassium is a soft, silvery alkali metal placed in Group 1 and Period 4 of the periodic table.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Potassium also has naturally occurring isotopes Potassium-40 (radioactive, used in K-Ar dating) and Potassium-41.

 

• Potassium's chemical symbol K comes from its Latin/Neo-Latin name Kalium.

 

NOTE

 

• 40 (Option 2): This is the mass number of the radioactive isotope Potassium-40, not the most common isotope.

 

• 38 (Option 3): Not a naturally significant isotope of potassium.

 

• 37 (Option 4): Not the mass number of potassium; too low given its atomic number of 19.

question: As of April 2022, who among the following musicians is NOT a recipient of the Bharat Ratna?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Zakir Hussain.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As of April 2022, Ustad Zakir Hussain (the renowned tabla maestro) had not been awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honour. (भारत रत्न — जाकिर हुसैन को नहीं मिला था)

 

• Pandit Ravi Shankar (sitar maestro) was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1999.

 

• Ustad Bismillah Khan (shehnai maestro) was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001.

 

• Lata Mangeshkar (playback singer) was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001; she passed away in February 2022.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Zakir Hussain received the Padma Shri (1988), Padma Bhushan (2002), and Padma Vibhushan (2023), but never the Bharat Ratna.

 

• The Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian award, instituted in 1954, and has been conferred on very few musicians overall, reflecting its rarity.

 

NOTE

 

• Ravi Shankar (Option 2): Received the Bharat Ratna in 1999.

 

• Bismillah Khan (Option 3): Received the Bharat Ratna in 2001.

 

• Lata Mangeshkar (Option 4): Received the Bharat Ratna in 2001.

question: What do you call the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Secondary productivity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Secondary productivity refers to the rate of formation of new organic (biomass) matter by consumers (heterotrophs) — the herbivores, carnivores and decomposers that feed on producers or other consumers. (द्वितीयक उत्पादकता — उपभोक्ताओं द्वारा)

 

• It contrasts with primary productivity, which is the rate at which producers (autotrophs, mainly green plants) convert solar energy into chemical/organic matter through photosynthesis.

 

• Secondary productivity depends on the amount of primary productivity available, since consumers derive their energy by consuming producers or other consumers along the food chain.

 

• Ecologists study secondary productivity to understand energy transfer efficiency between trophic levels in an ecosystem.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) is the total rate of photosynthesis, while Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is GPP minus respiration losses by producers.

 

• Only about 10% of energy typically transfers from one trophic level to the next (the 10% law), which is why secondary productivity is always much lower than primary productivity.

 

NOTE

 

• Tertiary productivity (Option 1): Not a standard term used in ecology for this concept.

 

• Primary productivity (Option 2): Refers to organic matter formation by producers, not consumers.

 

• Net productivity (Option 3): Refers to the productivity remaining after respiratory losses are subtracted, not specifically the rate of new organic matter formed by consumers.

question: Quwwat al-Islam mosque and minaret, built during the last decade of the ______ century.
solution_text:
The correct answer is twelth (twelfth).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque was commissioned by Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1192-93 CE, right after the establishment of the Delhi Sultanate, and its adjoining Qutub Minar was begun around 1199 CE — both falling in the last decade of the 12th (twelfth) century. (कुव्वत-उल-इस्लाम मस्जिद — बारहवीं शताब्दी)

 

• It is regarded as the first mosque built in India by the Delhi Sultans, constructed using materials from demolished Hindu and Jain temples, giving it a distinctive blend of Islamic and indigenous architectural styles.

 

• The Qutub Minar, begun by Aibak and later completed (with additional storeys) by his successor Iltutmish, stands adjacent to this mosque in the Qutub complex, Mehrauli, Delhi.

 

• The Qutub complex, including the mosque and minar, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Qutub Minar is the tallest brick minaret in the world, standing at about 73 metres.

 

• The mosque's courtyard contains the famous Iron Pillar of Delhi, dating to the Gupta period, which has remained largely rust-resistant for over 1,600 years.

 

NOTE

 

• Eleventh (Option 1): Too early; the mosque and minaret were built in the 1190s, in the twelfth century, not the eleventh.

 

• Thirteenth (Option 2): Too late; construction began in the last decade of the twelfth century (1190s), though completion by Iltutmish extended slightly into the thirteenth.

 

• Fourteenth (Option 3): Far too late; this does not correspond to the mosque's or minaret's initial construction period.

question: What is the structure of the Indian judiciary?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Four-tier.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian judiciary follows an integrated, four-tier structure: the Supreme Court at the apex, followed by High Courts at the state level, then District Courts, and finally Subordinate/Lower Courts below the district level. (भारतीय न्यायपालिका — चार-स्तरीय संरचना)

 

• The Supreme Court of India, headquartered in New Delhi, is the highest court and the final court of appeal in the country.

 

• High Courts are the principal civil courts of original jurisdiction in each state (or group of states/UTs), and sit at the second tier below the Supreme Court.

 

• District Courts and the further Subordinate Courts (Civil Judge courts, Judicial Magistrate courts, etc.) form the third and fourth tiers, handling cases at the district and lower administrative levels.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has a single integrated judicial system, unlike some federal countries that maintain separate parallel state and central court systems.

 

• Below the formal court hierarchy, Gram Nyayalayas and Lok Adalats provide additional avenues for speedy and alternative dispute resolution.

 

NOTE

 

• Two-tier (Option 2): Understates the actual number of distinct levels present in the Indian court hierarchy.

 

• Three-tier (Option 3): A commonly cited simplification (Supreme Court, High Courts, Subordinate Courts), but the standard/official description recognises District Courts as a distinct fourth tier.

 

• Five-tier (Option 4): Overstates the number of formal tiers in the standard description of the Indian judicial structure.

question: Who took charge as the chairman of The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India in March 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Debasish Panda.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Debasish Panda, a 1987-batch IAS officer, took charge as Chairman of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) in March 2022. (आईआरडीएआई अध्यक्ष — देबाशीष पांडा)

 

• Prior to this appointment, Debasish Panda served as the Secretary, Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance, Government of India.

 

• IRDAI is the statutory regulatory body for the insurance industry in India, established under the IRDA Act, 1999, and headquartered in Hyderabad, Telangana.

 

• As Chairman, Debasish Panda has overseen reforms aimed at increasing insurance penetration and pursuing the goal of "Insurance for All" by 2047.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• IRDAI was constituted following the recommendations of the Malhotra Committee (1994) on insurance sector reforms.

 

• The IRDAI regulates both life insurance and general (non-life) insurance companies operating in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Ajay Bhushan Pandey (Option 2): A former Finance Secretary and Revenue Secretary of India, not the IRDAI Chairman appointed in March 2022.

 

• Sanjeev Sanyal (Option 3): An economist who served as a member of the Economic Advisory Council to the PM (EAC-PM), not IRDAI Chairman.

 

• Ashwin Yardi (Option 4): A prominent insurance-industry executive (former CEO of Bajaj Allianz Life), not the IRDAI Chairman.

question: ______ is a city located on the confluence of river Yamuna and Ganga.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Allahabad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Allahabad (officially renamed Prayagraj in 2018), in Uttar Pradesh, is located at the confluence (Sangam) of the rivers Ganga, Yamuna and the mythical Saraswati. (संगम — प्रयागराज/इलाहाबाद)

 

• This confluence, known as the Triveni Sangam, is one of the most sacred sites in Hinduism and is the venue for the periodic Kumbh Mela, one of the largest religious gatherings in the world.

 

• Allahabad/Prayagraj has historically been an important political, administrative and cultural centre, and was also the site of the Allahabad High Court.

 

• The city's ancient name Prayag literally means "place of sacrifice/confluence" in Sanskrit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ardh Kumbh Mela is held at Prayagraj every 6 years, and the Maha Kumbh Mela every 12 years, alternating among Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain and Nashik.

 

• The Yamuna river itself originates from the Yamunotri Glacier in Uttarakhand and merges into the Ganga at Prayagraj after flowing through Delhi, Mathura and Agra.

 

NOTE

 

• Agra (Option 2): Located on the banks of the river Yamuna alone, not at its confluence with the Ganga; famous for the Taj Mahal.

 

• Kanpur (Option 3): Situated on the banks of the Ganga alone, not at a confluence with the Yamuna.

 

• Lucknow (Option 4): Situated on the banks of the Gomti river, not at the Ganga-Yamuna confluence.

question: Where was the FIH Women’s Indoor Hockey World Cup 2015 held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Leipzig, Germany.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The FIH Indoor Hockey World Cup 2015, for both the men's and women's categories, was held in Leipzig, Germany. (इनडोर हॉकी विश्व कप 2015 — लीपज़िग, जर्मनी)

 

• Indoor hockey is a variant of field hockey played on a smaller, hard indoor court, typically with modified rules (e.g., no lifting/hitting the ball hard, fewer players per side).

 

• The tournament is organised by the International Hockey Federation (FIH), the sport's global governing body.

 

• Germany has traditionally been a strong indoor hockey nation, and Leipzig has hosted major indoor hockey events.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Field hockey's flagship event, the Men's/Women's Hockey World Cup (outdoor), is a separate, larger tournament also organised by the FIH.

 

• India has a strong tradition in outdoor field hockey, having won multiple Olympic gold medals, though indoor hockey is a less prominent format for the country internationally.

 

NOTE

 

• Vienna, Austria (Option 1): Not the host city of the FIH Indoor Hockey World Cup 2015.

 

• Poznan, Poland (Option 2): Not the host city of the FIH Indoor Hockey World Cup 2015.

 

• Berlin, Germany (Option 4): Incorrect city within Germany; the tournament was hosted in Leipzig, not Berlin.

question: Which enzyme in the pancreatic juice helps in breaking down fats?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lipase.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pancreatic lipase is the enzyme secreted in the pancreatic juice that breaks down fats (lipids) into fatty acids and glycerol in the small intestine. (लाइपेज़ — वसा का पाचन)

 

• The pancreas is both an exocrine and endocrine gland; as an exocrine gland, it secretes pancreatic juice containing digestive enzymes into the duodenum via the pancreatic duct.

 

• Pancreatic juice contains three main types of enzymes: lipase (for fats), amylase (for carbohydrates), and proteases like trypsin and chymotrypsin (for proteins).

 

• Bile from the liver/gallbladder first emulsifies fats into smaller droplets, increasing the surface area for pancreatic lipase to act on efficiently.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pepsin is a protein-digesting enzyme secreted by the stomach (gastric glands), not the pancreas.

 

• Trypsin and chymotrypsin, secreted by the pancreas, digest proteins, while pancreatic amylase digests starch/carbohydrates.

 

NOTE

 

• Protease (Option 1): A general term for enzymes that digest proteins, not fats.

 

• Pepsin (Option 2): A protein-digesting enzyme secreted in the stomach, not the pancreas, and it does not act on fats.

 

• Amylase (Option 4): Digests carbohydrates/starch, not fats.

question: Who was the recipient of the National Devdasi Award in 2016?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prerana Deshpande.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Prerana Deshpande, an internationally acclaimed Kathak dancer and senior disciple of the Kathak maestro Dr. Rohini Bhate, was the recipient of the National Devdasi Award in 2016. (राष्ट्रीय देवदासी पुरस्कार 2016 — प्रेरणा देशपांडे)

 

• She is regarded as one of the leading solo Kathak performers of her generation, noted for her command over rhythm (laya), grace (bhava) and expression (abhinaya).

 

• Prerana Deshpande regularly performs at major classical dance festivals in India and internationally and is recognised for her contributions to preserving and popularising the Kathak tradition.

 

• This question is drawn from the SSC CGL 2022 Tier-I exam, tested on 08 December 2022.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• R. Muthukannammal, often referred to as one of India's last surviving traditional Devadasi (Sadir) dancers from Tamil Nadu, was separately honoured with the Padma Shri in 2022.

 

• Kathak, the classical dance form associated with Prerana Deshpande, originated in North India and is characterised by intricate footwork, spins (chakkars), and storytelling through mime.

 

NOTE

 

• Geeta Kapoor (Option 1): A well-known Bollywood choreographer and reality-show judge, not associated with the National Devdasi Award.

 

• R Muthukannammal (Option 2): A veteran Sadir/Devadasi-tradition dancer honoured separately with the Padma Shri, but not the 2016 National Devdasi Award recipient referenced here.

 

• Dr Sohini Ray (Option 4): Not the recipient of the National Devdasi Award in 2016.

question: Name the two states in which land reform were successful?
solution_text:
The correct answer is West Bengal and Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Among Indian states, land reforms are considered to have been implemented most successfully in West Bengal and Kerala. (भूमि सुधार — पश्चिम बंगाल और केरल)

 

• In West Bengal, the landmark "Operation Barga" (launched in 1978) recorded and protected the rights of bargadars (sharecroppers), giving them greater security of tenure and a fairer share of produce.

 

• Kerala implemented strong land reform legislation (notably the Kerala Land Reforms Act) that abolished intermediary tenures (like the Janmi-Kudiyan system) and redistributed surplus land, achieving one of the most effective land reform outcomes in India.

 

• Strong political will, effective land records, and grassroots mobilisation (often through Left-led governments) are cited as key reasons for the comparative success of land reforms in these two states.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Land reform measures generally included abolition of intermediaries (zamindari abolition), tenancy reforms, and imposition of land ceilings with redistribution of surplus land.

 

• In most other Indian states, land reforms are widely regarded as only partially successful, hampered by weak implementation, litigation, and loopholes exploited by large landholders.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttar Pradesh and Bihar (Option 1): Land reforms in these states are generally regarded as having achieved only limited success.

 

• Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu (Option 3): Not typically cited as the states with the most successful land reform outcomes.

 

• Karnataka and West Bengal (Option 4): While West Bengal saw successful reforms, Karnataka is not paired with it as the standard example; the standard pairing is West Bengal and Kerala.

question: In which game/sport is the area of bout called a ring?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Boxing.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Boxing, the square area in which a bout (match) is contested is called a "ring" (also called a "boxing ring"), typically enclosed by ropes on all four sides. (बॉक्सिंग रिंग — मुक्केबाज़ी का क्षेत्र)

 

• The term "ring" is a traditional term retained from early boxing history, even though the modern boxing area is square, not circular.

 

• A standard boxing ring is elevated on a platform and bounded by ropes attached to corner posts, distinguishing it clearly from the flat mat-based playing areas of other combat sports.

 

• Boxing is contested over a fixed number of rounds, with judges scoring based on clean punches landed, defence and ring generalship.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Boxing has been part of the Olympic Games since 1904 (men) and 2012 (women).

 

• Amateur boxing (as in the Olympics) differs from professional boxing in scoring methods, protective gear, and number/duration of rounds.

 

NOTE

 

• Taekwondo (Option 1): Contested on a flat, matted competition area, not called a "ring".

 

• Judo (Option 2): Played on a "tatami" mat area, not a ring.

 

• Karate (Option 3): Contested on a mat-based competition area, not called a ring.

question: According to census 2011, which state has lowest literacy rate in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Census 2011, Bihar recorded the lowest literacy rate among all Indian states, at approximately 63.82%. (जनगणना 2011 — बिहार सबसे कम साक्षरता दर)

 

• Bihar's literacy rate remained below the national average of 74.04% (Census 2011), reflecting persistent challenges in access to education, particularly in rural areas.

 

• In contrast, Kerala recorded the highest literacy rate among states, at about 93.91%, in the same census.

 

• Literacy rate, as measured by the Census, is defined as the percentage of the population aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding in any language.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Among Union Territories, Lakshadweep actually has one of the highest literacy rates (around 91-92%), not the lowest — it is a common distractor in such questions.

 

• Mizoram also has a comparatively high literacy rate (around 91%) among northeastern states.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 1): Had a literacy rate around 67-69% in Census 2011 — low, but higher than Bihar's.

 

• Lakshadweep (Option 2): Recorded one of the highest literacy rates in India (Census 2011), not the lowest.

 

• Mizoram (Option 3): Recorded a comparatively high literacy rate in Census 2011, not the lowest.

question: Ekaharya is the solo artist in which Indian classical dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Ekaharya" refers to a solo performance style where a single dancer portrays multiple characters/roles within one piece, and this concept is closely associated with Bharatanatyam. (एकहार्य अभिनय — भरतनाट्यम)

 

• In this format, the solo dancer uses abhinaya (expressive gestures, facial expressions and body movement) to switch between different characters in a narrative, without changing costume.

 

• Bharatanatyam, one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originated in the temples of Tamil Nadu and is traditionally performed as a solo recital.

 

• The concept of Ekaharya is rooted in ancient Indian dramaturgy, referenced in texts like the Natya Shastra, describing a single performer embodying several dramatic roles.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bharatanatyam's traditional repertoire (margam) includes items like Alarippu, Jatiswaram, Shabdam, Varnam, Padam, Tillana, performed in sequence.

 

• Other major Indian classical dance forms include Kathak (North India), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Mohiniyattam and Kathakali (Kerala), and Sattriya (Assam).

 

NOTE

 

• Kathak (Option 1): A North Indian classical dance form known for rhythmic footwork and spins (chakkars), not specifically associated with the term "Ekaharya".

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 3): A classical dance-drama form from Andhra Pradesh, traditionally more group/drama-oriented in its origins, not the form specifically linked to "Ekaharya".

 

• Mohiniyattam (Option 4): A graceful solo dance form from Kerala, but not the one specifically associated with the term "Ekaharya".

question: Who has taken over as President of Financial Action Task Force in July 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is T Raja Kumar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• T. Raja Kumar of Singapore took over as President of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) for a two-year term beginning 1 July 2022. (एफएटीएफ अध्यक्ष — टी. राजा कुमार, सिंगापुर)

 

• He succeeded Dr. Marcus Pleyer of Germany, who had served as FATF President for the preceding term.

 

• The FATF is an inter-governmental body established in 1989 that sets global standards and promotes effective measures for combating money laundering, terrorist financing, and proliferation financing.

 

• The FATF Presidency rotates among member jurisdictions and typically runs on fixed-term cycles.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The FATF is headquartered in Paris, France, and India has been a member of the FATF since 2010.

 

• Countries placed on the FATF "grey list" face increased monitoring due to deficiencies in their anti-money laundering/counter-terrorism financing frameworks.

 

NOTE

 

• Sanjiv Kapoor (Option 2): Not the FATF President appointed in July 2022.

 

• Ashwani Bhatia (Option 3): An Indian financial-sector executive (associated with SBI Mutual Fund/SEBI), not the FATF President.

 

• Mahesh Verma (Option 4): Not the FATF President appointed in July 2022.

question: Salamander belongs to which of the following classes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amphibian.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Salamanders belong to the class Amphibia, order Urodela (Caudata), which comprises amphibians that retain a tail into adulthood. (सैलामैंडर — उभयचर वर्ग)

 

• Like other amphibians, salamanders typically have a life cycle involving both aquatic (larval, gill-breathing) and terrestrial (adult, lung/skin-breathing) stages.

 

• Salamanders have moist, glandular skin (used for cutaneous respiration) and are ectothermic (cold-blooded), consistent with the defining features of Class Amphibia.

 

• Other well-known amphibians include frogs and toads (order Anura) and caecilians (order Gymnophiona/Apoda), which are legless, burrowing amphibians.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Amphibians are considered evolutionary intermediates between fully aquatic fish and fully terrestrial reptiles, reflecting their dual aquatic-terrestrial life stages.

 

• Salamanders are notable among vertebrates for their strong ability to regenerate lost limbs and tissues.

 

NOTE

 

• Pieces (Option 1): A misspelling of "Pisces" (the fish class); salamanders are not fish.

 

• Reptiles (Option 2): Reptiles (Class Reptilia) are distinct from amphibians — they have dry, scaly skin and lay amniotic eggs, unlike salamanders.

 

• Aves (Option 3): The class of birds; salamanders are not birds.

question: Which festival is celebrated on the last day of the holy month of Ramadan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Eid-ul-Fitr.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Eid-ul-Fitr (also spelled Eid al-Fitr) marks the end of the holy month of Ramadan, the month of fasting observed by Muslims. (ईद-उल-फ़ित्र — रमज़ान के अंत का त्योहार)

 

• It is celebrated on the first day of the Islamic month of Shawwal, immediately following the completion of the 29 or 30 days of fasting during Ramadan.

 

• Celebrations typically include special congregational prayers (Eid Namaz), charity (Zakat-al-Fitr) given to the needy before the prayers, festive meals, and the exchange of greetings and gifts among family and friends.

 

• Eid-ul-Fitr is often referred to as the "Festival of Breaking the Fast".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Eid-ul-Zuha (Eid al-Adha), also called Bakrid, is the "Festival of Sacrifice", commemorating Prophet Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice his son, and is celebrated about two months after Eid-ul-Fitr.

 

• Milad-un-Nabi commemorates the birth anniversary of Prophet Muhammad, and Shab-e-Barat is a night of prayer and remembrance observed in the month of Shaban, roughly two weeks before Ramadan begins.

 

NOTE

 

• Milad-un-Nabi (Option 1): Commemorates the Prophet Muhammad's birthday, not the end of Ramadan.

 

• Shab-e-Barat (Option 3): Observed in the month of Shaban, before Ramadan starts, not marking its end.

 

• Eid-ul-zuha (Option 4): The "Festival of Sacrifice" (Bakrid), celebrated separately in the month of Dhu al-Hijjah, unrelated to the end of Ramadan.

question: The craftspersons of Bidar were so famed for their inlay work in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Copper and Silver.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The craftspersons of Bidar (in present-day Karnataka) were famed for their inlay work in copper and silver, a metalwork tradition that came to be known as "Bidri" (or Bidriware) after the town. (बीदर — तांबे और चांदी की जड़ाई कारीगरी, बिदरी)

 

• Bidriware involves inlaying fine silver (and sometimes copper) wire/sheet designs onto a blackened base of zinc and copper alloy, producing striking black-and-silver decorative objects such as vases, hookah bases and boxes.

 

• This distinctive craft technique gave rise to the very term "Bidri", directly derived from the town's name, Bidar.

 

• This is a well-known reference point in Indian history/craft studies (drawn from NCERT-level material on medieval Indian crafts and towns).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bidriware received a Geographical Indication (GI) tag, recognising it as a craft unique to the Bidar region.

 

• Other historic Indian towns were similarly famed for particular crafts — e.g., Bengal for muslin, Gujarat for silk and cotton weaving.

 

NOTE

 

• Gold and Bronze (Option 1): Not the metals associated with Bidar's traditional inlay craft.

 

• Bronze and Silver (Option 2): Bronze is not the metal historically paired with silver in Bidar's inlay craft; the standard pairing is copper and silver.

 

• Gold and Copper (Option 3): Gold is not the metal historically associated with Bidar's inlay craft; silver, not gold, is paired with copper.

question: The group of islands which form part of India and lie to the southeast of Indian mainland in Bay of Bengal is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andaman and Nicobar islands.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands form a group of islands lying in the Bay of Bengal, to the southeast of the Indian mainland, and constitute a Union Territory of India. (अंडमान और निकोबार द्वीप समूह — बंगाल की खाड़ी)

 

• The archipelago comprises around 572 islands, of which only a small fraction are inhabited, with Port Blair as its capital.

 

• The Andaman group lies to the north and the Nicobar group to the south, separated by the Ten Degree Channel.

 

• These islands are of great strategic and ecological importance, home to unique tribal groups (e.g., Sentinelese, Jarawa) and rich coral reef biodiversity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Lakshadweep Islands, in contrast, lie in the Arabian Sea, to the southwest of the Indian mainland (off the coast of Kerala) — the geographic opposite of the Andaman and Nicobar group.

 

• Indira Point, on Great Nicobar Island, is the southernmost point of India.

 

NOTE

 

• Lakshadweep islands (Option 1): Located in the Arabian Sea, to the southwest of the mainland, not the Bay of Bengal/southeast.

 

• Mannar island (Option 3): A single island (Rameswaram/Mannar area) near the India-Sri Lanka strait, not a large island group in the Bay of Bengal southeast of India.

 

• Maldive islands (Option 4): An independent island nation southwest of India in the Indian Ocean, not part of India.
